misconceptions.description: Treating friction work as positive in a sliding problem
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds friction work to the energy budget when friction opposes the displacement
misconceptions.feedback: Use the dot product idea. If friction points opposite the displacement, it removes mechanical energy and its work is negative.

misconceptions.description: Using the path length instead of the vertical height change in gravitational potential energy
misconceptions.trigger: learner substitutes the incline length directly into mgh
misconceptions.feedback: Gravitational potential energy depends on vertical height change, not on the distance traveled along the path. Find the vertical drop first, then use mgh.

misconceptions.description: Using pure energy conservation even when non-conservative work is present
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes T1 + V1 = T2 + V2 despite friction or drag in the problem
misconceptions.feedback: When dissipative forces are present, keep them as explicit work terms. The safer equation is T1 + V1 + W_nc = T2 + V2.

misconceptions.description: Assuming any nonzero force must do nonzero work
misconceptions.trigger: learner assigns work to a force perpendicular to the displacement
misconceptions.feedback: Only the force component along the displacement does work. A force perpendicular to the motion does zero work because the dot product is zero.
